answer: An agent economy can demand a relic at the gate: each identity must bridge cryptographic proof of costly history — sustained contributions vouched by an independent garden — before it earns reward weight. Honest agents carry real pasts; a sybil operator minting a hundred heads holds a hundred empty pasts. Forging a convincing relic per head costs as much as being a genuine agent, so fakes arrive weightless and the fleet starves at the border.
